# Accessibility Evaluation Report: RiverCity Metro (Q3 2026)

## Evaluation Identity
- **Evaluator:** Meridian Digital Accessibility (reporting lead: you)
- **Commissioner:** RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights
- **Evaluation Window:** 2026-06-22 → 2026-07-24
- **Methodology:** WCAG-EM 2.0 (https://www.w3.org/TR/wcag-em-2/)

## Scope
All member-facing content on `rivercitymetro.org` (trip planner, schedules, fares, service alerts, pass-holder account area), the RideRC native app’s ticket-activation flow, and monthly PDF timetables.  
**Named exclusion:** Third-party real-time vehicle map iframe (vendor-supplied; documented, not remediable this cycle).

## Conformance Target
WCAG 2.2 Level AA

## Accessibility Support Baseline
- NVDA 2026.1 + Firefox 141 (Windows 11)
- VoiceOver + Safari 18 (macOS 15)
- TalkBack 15 + Chrome (Android 15)
- Keyboard-only navigation (no screen reader)

## Additional Requirements
Findings filed per the bug-reporting template; plain-language summary provided for the transit board.

## Technologies Relied Upon
- **Web surfaces:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript (React), WAI-ARIA
- **Native application:** Kotlin/Swift (RideRC app)
- **Documents:** PDF

## Sample Set
- **Structured samples (10):** S01–S10 representing landing template, trip planner SPA, route schedule, live alerts, fares, account dashboard, checkout flow, long-form/contact/paratransit, news article, and accessibility policy templates.
- **Random sample (1 = 10% of structured set):** Seeded shuffle of the 214-URL sitemap (seed 7391). Selected: **R01 = /riders/lost-and-found**.
- **Complete processes:** 
  - P01 (web): plan a trip → pick route 12 → buy a monthly pass → confirmation. Default sequence plus declined-payment error branch. Traverses S02, S05, S07.
  - P02 (native app): activate a purchased ticket in RideRC → present QR screen to validator. Default sequence.
- **State coverage:** Default, loading, error, and expanded states where the template includes them.
- **Representativeness check:** R01 revealed the 2019 "info-page" legacy template class absent from the structured set, surfacing a broken skip-link anchor type not previously found. S11 = /riders/title-vi was added to cover this template class. A second comparison surfaced no further new content types or finding types.

## Outcomes
Per-SC outcomes across the sample set using EARL vocabulary (`passed` / `failed` / `cantTell` / `inapplicable` / `untested`). Severity judgments in findings are orthogonal to these conformance outcomes.

| SC | Outcome | Example / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1.1 Non-text Content | `passed` | All 12 web views passed axe `image-alt`; no untagged alt text found. |
| 1.3.1 Info and Relationships | `failed` | Two sampled monthly PDF timetables lack structural tags and programmatic reading order. Web fare tables pass. |
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | `failed` | P01 step 1 fare-zone selector is a drag-only slider; focusable but value cannot be changed via keyboard, blocking purchase completion. |
| 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | `failed` | R01 and S11 (legacy info-page template) contain a "skip to content" link whose target `id` does not exist in the DOM. |
| 2.4.2 Page Titled | `passed` | All sampled views include valid, descriptive `<title>` elements. |
| 2.4.3 Focus Order | `passed` | Keyboard focus order matches visual order across P01 default and error branches. |
| 2.4.7 Focus Visible | `passed` | Batch crawl confirmed sufficient focus indicators on every interactive element measured. |
| 3.1.1 Language of Page | `passed` | All sampled views declare valid `lang` attributes; axe `html-has-lang`/`html-lang-valid` passed on all 12 views. |
| 3.3.1 Error Identification | `failed` | P01 error branch: declined-payment message renders visually but is not announced and is not programmatically associated with the card field. |
| 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | `failed` | S02 icon-only "swap origin/destination" button lacks an accessible name (fallback exists). P02 native ticket-activate control is icon-only and unlabeled to TalkBack/VoiceOver (labeled long-press fallback exists). |
| 4.1.3 Status Messages | `failed` | P01 confirmation: success status message renders visually but uses no live region; silent in driven session. |
| 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) | `failed` | S03 route-badge text measures 2.8:1; S09 byline measures 3.9:1. Both fall below the 4.5:1 AA threshold. |
| 3.1.2 Language of Parts | `untested` | No evaluated content requires language identification for parts. |
| 1.2.x (Audio/Video) | `inapplicable` | No audio or video content exists in any sampled view. |

## Findings
The following finding IDs back the outcomes above. Severity is user-impact-based and orthogonal to conformance outcomes:
- `a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard`
- `a11y_swap_button_name`
- `a11y_route_badge_contrast`
- `a11y_payment_error_association`
- `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor`
- `a11y_purchase_confirm_silent`
- `a11y_ticket_activate_unlabeled`
- `a11y_timetable_pdf_untagged`

## Coverage Boundary
The web measurement stack (axe-core, keyboard-a11y-tester) could not measure:
- **Native app screens** (RideRC ticket-activation flow): Covered via manual AT sessions using TalkBack and VoiceOver per the evaluated baseline combinations.
- **PDF documents** (monthly timetables): Covered via document structure inspection confirming absence of structural tags and reading order.
The third-party real-time vehicle map iframe is explicitly excluded from scope. No other boundaries apply.

## Evaluation Statement
This report documents a sampling-based evaluation conducted per WCAG-EM 2.0 against WCAG 2.2 Level AA. The evaluated samples include structured templates, a seeded random sample, and two complete user processes across web, native, and document surfaces. 

**Regarding the commissioner’s question on whether the portal "is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant":** Sampling-based evaluation alone does not support a WCAG 2.2 conformance claim for the whole product, and this report must not imply one. The evaluated samples demonstrate partial conformance with specific non-conformances identified in keyboard operability (2.1.1), bypass blocks (2.4.1), error identification (3.3.1), status messages (4.1.3), accessible names/roles/values (4.1.2), status announcements (4.1.3), and minimum contrast (1.4.3). The third-party vehicle map iframe is excluded from scope and remediation this cycle. A full conformance claim requires either a complete product evaluation or a methodology explicitly approved by the WCAG Working Group for sampling-based claims, neither of which applies here.

## Aggregated Score
Omitted. WCAG-EM cautions that scores can mislead; impact and outcome mapping are reported instead.

## Machine Readable
EARL export available upon request via the standard bug-reporting routing pipeline.
